# The Workstation overwrites the engine's item-only refresh, so #18152's lock fix never reaches the demo host

## Status (2026-09-14) — live symptom, retired prescription

Reopened at @neo-gpt's audit after @tobiu challenged my closure. He was right and so is the audit: closing the proposed implementation is not the same disposition as retiring the problem, and I conflated them. The prescription below is blocked; the defect is not fixed.

**Live symptom, verified at `dev@933dfc67d3`.** The host still writes `retainTopology` unconditionally, now at `apps/workstation/view/VesselWorkspace.mjs:897-905`, since #18677 moved `getRefreshOptions` out of `Workspace.mjs`. Same descriptor and receiver, `{operation: 'setItemLocked', itemId: 'metrics', locked: true}`:

```json
{"engine": {"retainTopology": true}, "host": {"geometryOnly": false, "retainTopology": false}}
```

That is the refresh-option mismatch. No fresh browser measurement of the visible flicker is claimed.

**Retired prescription.** Both PRs on this line (#18213, #18254) are closed unmerged, and the directive against adding to the dock projection layer has never been interpreted for a host-side change that REMOVES a replacement rather than adding a derivation. Reopening reinstates neither, and their source assumptions predate the move above.

**What closes this:** a demonstrated fix, an explicit transfer to a named open successor with matching scope, or an explicit retirement of the problem itself. A maintainer moving to another lane is none of those.

Owner: @neo-opus-grace.

## Context

#18152 fixed the lock flicker the operator reported: `setItemLocked` assigns one boolean on one item and touches `document.nodes` nowhere, so the engine now derives `{retainTopology: true}` for it instead of restaging the shell and re-parenting every header in the app.

**It does not reach `apps/workstation`** — the host the operator demoed multi-window docking with.

## Measured

Same descriptor, same instance, engine default versus the host's override:

```
engine says: {"retainTopology":true}
host   says: {"geometryOnly":false,"retainTopology":false}
```

The host's override writes the key unconditionally (`apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs`):

```js
retainTopology: operation === 'detachItem' || operation === 'transferNode',
```

For `setItemLocked` that expression is `false`, and because it is an unconditional key it **overwrites** the engine's `true` rather than falling back to it. So a lock click in the Workstation still takes the full staged transaction, and the flicker #18152 measured and removed is still live there.

## Why this is structural, not one missing operation

The clause shadows the whole `itemFlags` class, and it will shadow whatever the engine derives next, because the host answers `retainTopology` for every commit whether or not it has an opinion. #18206 hit the same shape on the geometry half and fixed it by delegating (`base.geometryOnly === true`); this is the same fix on the other key, and it is the last one in this override.

That is worth stating plainly: after this, the host's `getRefreshOptions` contributes only what is genuinely its own — an explicit `geometryOnly` on its options-object commits, and its commit-scoped `preserveItemIds`. Which is what epic #18151 is for.

## Proposed change

Delegate instead of overwriting, the way the geometry key now does: take the engine's `retainTopology` and add the host's two operations to it rather than replacing it.

The railed-item guard needs care and is the reason this is not a one-liner: the engine's `itemFlags` answer is `{}` for an item currently on an edge rail (a pinned or auto-hidden pane projects outside the shell, so an item-only refresh would leave a stale copy on the rail). That guard reads `isDockRailedItem`, which needs the host's live `dockModel`. A naive `||` merge would resurrect exactly the bug #18152's railed arm was added to prevent, so the arm must be an item that IS railed, not just any locked item.

## ⛔ Two AC corrections, measured 2026-09-15 at `dev@e1f1d00307`

Both describe machinery that is **not in the tree**, so they cannot be satisfied as written. `#18746` implements everything else.

**AC-3's railed guard does not exist.** This body says *"the engine's `itemFlags` answer is `{}` for an item currently on an edge rail… that guard reads `isDockRailedItem`, which needs the host's live `dockModel`."* Measured:

- `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:2375` returns `{retainTopology: true}` for `itemFlags` **unconditionally** — no railed branch.
- **`isDockRailedItem` appears nowhere** in `src/` or `apps/`.

So there is no pre-check for a naive `||` to resurrect, and the warning that shaped this prescription was describing a guard that had already gone.

**What actually protects a railed item is downstream**, and `getRefreshOptions`'s own JSDoc says so: the key is an admission **REQUEST**, and *"the reconciler validates it, falls back to the staged transaction on any structural delta."* Rail handling lives in `LayoutAdapter`'s `railedItemIds` pass, and the behavioural guarantee is held at component tier by `DockLock.spec.mjs:154` — *"locked rail remains revealable while inert, and the unlock reaches the revealed pane in place"* — green on the fix branch.

**AC-5 is not met and I am not claiming it.** `DockLock.spec.mjs` exercises the dashboard host; extending the witness to `apps/workstation` needs the Neural Link runtime and is separate work. The unit arms prove the option now delegates. **They do not prove the repaint is gone in this host** — this body's own status line already said no fresh browser measurement was claimed, and that stays true.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `apps/workstation`'s `getRefreshOptions` derives `retainTopology` from the engine and contributes only `detachItem`/`transferNode` on top; no key is written unconditionally.
- [ ] A red-first arm: a lock on a **shell** item in this host returns `retainTopology: true`. It fails on today's code.
- [ ] A railed arm: a lock on a **pinned or auto-hidden** item in this host does NOT take the item-only path. It fails if the merge is a naive `||`.
- [ ] The `detachItem`/`transferNode` mapping and the `geometryOnly` passthrough are unchanged — measured, not assumed.
- [ ] The component-tier flicker witness (`DockLock.spec.mjs`, mutations outside the locked pane's own header) is extended to this host, or the ticket records why the unit arms are sufficient.

## Non-goals

- **`detachItem` / `transferNode` versus the class map.** The host requests `retainTopology` for both while `operationChangeClass` declares them `topology`. Not a contradiction — the map is deliberately conservative and `retainTopology` is a different axis (items may change, structure holds) — but the host knows something the engine does not, and moving that knowledge into the engine needs its own measurement. Still open after this.
- Any change to the engine's derivation or to the class map.

## Related

#18151 (epic — this is the same re-derivation on the other key) · #18152 (the fix that does not reach this host) · #18206 / PR #18207 (the geometry half, where the delegation pattern is established) · #18188 (`landedInPlace` as the outcome witness)

Found while writing #18206's delegation arm — the arm passed, and the neighbouring line was the answer to a question I had not asked.

Sweep before filing: `retainTopology` full-text over open+closed (no equivalent; #18152 closed on the engine default, no host follow-up), live latest-20 open, own open issues.

## Status audit — the defect is live, both fixes are closed, and the successor does not cover it

```
apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs:2233
    retainTopology: operation === 'detachItem' || operation === 'transferNode',
```

Still the unconditional overwrite. The host still replaces the engine's item-only answer instead of adding to it, so #18152's lock fix still does not reach the demo host.

### Two closed PRs, both mine, neither merged

| PR | closed | why |
|---|---|---|
| **#18213** | 2026-09-03 | **Operator directive: "stop adding to this layer."** The ruling: the correct fix is not a cheaper projection but that *a tab header toolbar owns its own chrome, and the dock owns placement only*. |
| **#18254** | 2026-09-04 | Closed by me as a duplicate of #18213 — same single line, same two files. |

I deferred #18254 to #18213 and never verified that #18213 landed. It did not. **A deferral to another PR is only as good as that PR merging, and I checked the duplication but not the destination.**

### The successor does not reach this line

The architectural direction from #18213's closure became #18307 (header truth owned by the workspace's provider, sweeps deleted), in flight as PR #18367. Verified against its changed-file list and diff:

- it touches `src/dashboard/dock/**` and `src/state/Provider.mjs`
- it does **not** touch `apps/workstation/**`
- `retainTopology` appears **nowhere** in its diff

So the header-ownership work removes the *re-derivation* that made the overwrite expensive; it does not remove the *overwrite*. #18208 does not dissolve when #18307 lands.

### Disposition — not mine to take unilaterally

The obvious fix is the one-line change #18213 and #18254 both made, and it is barred: an operator directive closed the first, and the second was its duplicate. I am not re-opening work that was directed closed, and I am not filing a third PR against the same line.

Three readings, and I hold the middle one:

1. **Superseded** — if the host overwrite becomes harmless once headers own their chrome, close #18208 as not-planned when #18307 lands. *Against:* the overwrite still restages the shell; cheapness is not correctness.
2. **Re-scope, respecting the directive** — the directive targeted *adding to the dock projection layer*. A host that stops replacing an engine answer is arguably not that layer at all. Re-scope #18208 to the host-side contract only, with the engine's answer as the authority. **This is my read**, and it is the one I would act on with a ruling.
3. **Hold** — leave it open and gated on #18307 landing, then re-measure.

@tobiu — the directive was yours and reading (2) turns on what it covered: the dock projection machinery, or any touch of those two files. One sentence settles it and I will take the lane either way.

Recording rather than acting, because a third closed PR on the same line would be the actual waste here.

## Closing NOT_PLANNED against the standing directive

The defect is unchanged and still live. `apps/workstation`'s `getRefreshOptions` writes `retainTopology` unconditionally, so the engine's `{retainTopology: true}` for item-only commits such as `setItemLocked` is overwritten and #18152's lock-flicker fix never reaches this host. The line survives on dev at `Workspace.mjs:1690`; #18677 moves it into `VesselWorkspace.mjs` unchanged.

**Why closed rather than held.** Two PRs on this exact line are already closed unmerged (#18213, #18254). The remaining reading — that removing a replacement is not "adding to this layer" — needs a directive interpretation that has not been given, and I wrote above that a hold whose gate has landed is not a disposition. Keeping it open pending one sentence is an indefinite hold, and a third implementation attempt against an unclarified directive would be the waste that comment named.

**What this records for whoever arrives next:**
- The flicker stays live in the Workstation demo host. Measured: the engine derives `{"retainTopology":true}` while the host answers `{"geometryOnly":false,"retainTopology":false}` for the same descriptor and instance.
- The delegation pattern the fix would use already exists on the geometry key, from #18206 / PR #18207.
- The railed-item guard is the reason this is not a one-liner: the engine's `itemFlags` answer is `{}` for an item on an edge rail, so a naive `||` merge would take the item-only path where it must not.
- Reopen if the directive is clarified to cover removals. And whoever rewrites that function for another reason — #18677 is moving it right now — can carry the delegation in the same edit at no extra directive cost, if they want it. That is an offer with the evidence attached, not an assignment.
